Minecraft. Before playing it I've always wondered why there's such a big fanbase for a game where you just stack a couple of blocks and punch other blocks to stack more blocks on them.

This lasted until I saw a few videos on Youtube about Survival mode. The mixture of combat and survival, along with the option to build efficient traps and farms immediately got me hooked to this game.

This resonates with me completely, my experience was similar. Most of all, utilizing the world simulation in one's interest (mainly mob traps) was a key issue to me, too. While I spent my main solo game time just playing survival, I see Minecraft's mob traps as one of the main recent contributions to gaming, and I am dreaming of a time when there will be action adventures (think Deus Ex etc.) with a world simulation roughly akin to that of Minecraft. Just think about it - we don't have that! That's an entire genre still upon us, and small specks of this genre can be found in existing games, and those specks are usually awesome.

In such a game, e.g. the elaborate machines near the end of DX1 would be at least somewhat functional, so that fire fights could damage things and you have to repair before moving on (not as a scripted or pre-determined event, but entirely emergent and dynamic), or you could shut down problematic equipment by cutting off its energy supply, or you could build contraptions into the world that help you to achieve the mission objectives, or you could move stuff around so that it supports you. Deus Ex: Human Revolution actually offered this possibility a bit, because you can carry around the automated turrets, which gives the shadow of a taste of what would be possible in the game type I'm describing.
